Attempts to unify two unevaluated consts by first converting both into abstract consts. It explicitly calls `AbstractConst::new` for each input and, if both succeed, calls `try_unify`; any `ErrorReported` is conservatively treated as success via `unwrap_or_else`.

Traverses an `AbstractConst` in preorder, invoking a callback on each subtree. It explicitly calls the local helper `recurse`, which in turn uses `AbstractConst::root` and `AbstractConst::subtree` to descend through child nodes.

Structurally compares two abstract consts for unification, repeatedly expanding leaf unevaluated consts before matching node shapes and leaf values. Iteratively computes missing required where-clause bounds for generic associated types by intersecting constraints inferred from other trait items and diagnosing any still-missing outlives predicates; this method calls `gather_gat_bounds`, `augment_param_env`, `region_known_to_outlive`, and `ty_known_to_outlive` from the Methods List.

Tests whether a type is known to outlive a region under the current environment by solving region constraints with the supplied WF types; this method calls `resolve_regions_with_wf_tys` from the Methods List.

Tests whether one region is known to outlive another under the current environment by adding the corresponding subregion constraint and resolving regions; this method calls `resolve_regions_with_wf_tys` from the Methods List.

Creates a fresh inference context, derives implied bounds from the provided WF types, applies caller-supplied region constraints, resolves regions, and returns whether no errors were produced; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Constructs a fresh `GATSubstCollector`, visits a type-foldable value, and returns the collected non-late-bound region and type arguments used in projections of the target GAT; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Visits each type, and when it sees a projection of the target GAT, records its lifetime and type substitution arguments before continuing recursive traversal; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Recognizes whether a HIR type is a single-segment trait object naming the enclosing trait itself, which likely should have been written as `Self`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Detects trait items that refer to their own trait by name as an unboxed trait object in argument, return, const, or associated-type positions, and emits a `Self` replacement suggestion when the trait is object-unsafe; this method calls `could_be_self` from the Methods List.
Computes the relevant method signature/span for an impl item and delegates its WF checking as an associated item; this method calls `check_associated_item` from the Methods List.

Checks well-formedness restrictions on generic parameters, currently focusing on const parameters by rejecting non-structural-match or otherwise unsupported const-generic parameter types and emitting targeted diagnostics; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Runs WF checking for an associated const, function, or type by creating a checking context, determining the appropriate `Self` type, and then validating the item's type/signature/defaults as needed; this method calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `normalize`, `register_wf_obligation`, `check_associated_type_bounds`, and `tcx` from the Methods List.
Maps an HIR item kind to its corresponding ADT kind for structs, unions, and enums, or returns `None` for non-ADT items; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Checks a struct/union/enum definition by visiting its variants and fields, registering WF obligations for field types, enforcing `Sized`-related layout constraints, handling packed/drop-copy cases, checking const-evaluatability for enum discriminants where needed, and validating where-clauses; this method calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `register_wf_obligation`, `item_adt_kind`, and `check_where_clauses` from the Methods List.

Checks a trait or trait alias by rejecting associated items in marker traits, validating the trait's where-clauses in a WF context, and running extra GAT bound analysis for real traits; this method calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `check_where_clauses`, and `check_gat_where_clauses` from the Methods List.

Loads explicit bounds for a trait associated type, normalizes each bound, converts them into WF predicate obligations, and registers the resulting obligations; this method calls `tcx` and `normalize` from the Methods List.

Creates a WF checking context for a function item, retrieves its function signature, and delegates signature validation to the shared function/method checker; this method calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt` from the Methods List.

Checks the type of a static/const/foreign static by normalizing it, registering its WF obligation, requiring `Sized` unless a foreign tail type is allowed, and requiring `Sync` for eligible shared statics; this method calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `normalize`, and `register_wf_obligation` from the Methods List.

Checks an impl by entering a WF context, validating either the implemented trait reference via trait obligations or the self type directly for inherent impls, and then checking the impl's where-clauses; this method calls `enter_wf_checking_ctxt`, `normalize`, `register_wf_obligation`, and `check_where_clauses` from the Methods List.

Validates where-clauses and generic defaults for an item by checking concrete default type/const arguments for WF, analyzing which predicates mention the item's own parameters, normalizing and instantiating relevant predicates, and registering the resulting WF obligations; this method calls `tcx` and `register_wf_obligation` from the Methods List.

Performs well-formedness checking for a function or method signature by liberating late-bound regions, normalizing each input/output component separately, registering WF obligations for every parameter and the return type, checking the item's where-clauses, and validating RPITIT bounds on the return type. Validates a method's `self` receiver type by normalizing the method signature, `Self` type, and receiver type, then checking receiver legality with or without `arbitrary_self_types` and emitting either the standard invalid-receiver error or a feature-gate error as appropriate. Checks whether a method receiver type is a valid form of `self` by first allowing direct equality with `Self`, then autodereferencing the receiver until it can be equated with `Self`, registering autoderef obligations on success, and—when `arbitrary_self_types` is disabled—requiring each deref step to implement the `Receiver` trait. This method calls `receiver_is_implemented` from the Methods List.

Tests whether a candidate receiver type satisfies the lang-item `Receiver` trait by building a trait obligation and querying whether it must hold modulo regions. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Checks a type definition for unused/bivariant generic parameters by collecting parameters constrained by non-bivariant variance or predicates, lazily computing which parameters are explicitly bounded in HIR, and reporting each remaining unconstrained parameter. Builds and emits the unused-parameter diagnostic for a bivariant generic parameter, including marker-type and possible const-parameter suggestions when applicable. This method calls `error_392` from the Methods List.
Creates the base E0392 diagnostic for an unused generic parameter and labels the parameter span as unused. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Builds a temporary `FnCtxt` inside the inherited context, optionally calls `check_false_global_bounds`, then invokes the supplied closure to gather WF types and finishes by calling `select_all_obligations_or_error` and `regionck_item`.

Top-level item WF dispatcher: inspects the HIR item kind and routes checking to the appropriate helper. Handles binders during GAT substitution collection by calling `liberate_late_bound_regions` on the binder clone and then recursively visiting the liberated value with `visit_with`.
Creates a `CheckWfFcxBuilder` for an HIR item by calling `for_id` with the item's def-id and span.
Constructs a `CheckWfFcxBuilder` for a specific owner using `Inherited::build`, `hir::HirId::make_owner`, and `tcx.param_env`.
Records encountered type parameters by inserting `ty::Param` indices into the set, then continues recursive traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.
Stops traversal at regions by immediately returning `ControlFlow::BREAK` and calling no other listed methods.
Records encountered const parameters by inserting `ConstKind::Param` indices into the set, then continues recursive traversal by calling `super_visit_with`.

Checks elaborated predicates under an empty param environment for trivially false global bounds: it elaborates predicates, normalizes eligible global predicates, registers them as obligations, and finally calls `select_all_obligations_or_error`.
Constructs a `CheckTypeWellFormedVisitor` from the given `TyCtxt` and calls no other listed methods.
Parallel visitor entry for items that clones the visitor and forwards to `Visitor::visit_item`.

Parallel visitor entry for foreign items that clones the visitor and forwards to `Visitor::visit_foreign_item`.
Supplies the HIR nested visit map by returning `self.tcx.hir()`.
Visits an item by forcing `check_item_well_formed` through `tcx.ensure()` and then continuing traversal with `hir_visit::walk_item`.
Visits a trait item by forcing `check_trait_item_well_formed` through `tcx.ensure()` and then continuing traversal with `hir_visit::walk_trait_item`.
Visits an impl item by forcing `check_impl_item_well_formed` through `tcx.ensure()` and then continuing traversal with `hir_visit::walk_impl_item`.
Checks the well-formedness of a generic parameter by calling `check_param_wf`, then continues traversal with `hir_visit::walk_generic_param`.

Builds an `AdtVariant` for a struct/union-like variant by iterating fields, fetching each field type, calling `normalize_associated_types_in`, then `resolve_vars_if_possible`, and collecting the resulting `AdtField`s.
Builds `AdtVariant` data for every enum variant by iterating variants and calling `non_enum_variant` for each variant's fields while also recording explicit discriminant def-ids.

Computes the set of types contributing implied bounds for an impl: for trait impls it calls `normalize_associated_types_in` on the trait ref and collects its substituted types, and for inherent impls it calls `normalize_associated_types_in` on `self` type and returns that singleton set.

Resolves an `mir::UnevaluatedConst` under the given parameter environment after rejecting inference-containing args; on successful `ty::Instance::resolve`, it creates a `GlobalId` and calls `const_eval_global_id`, otherwise returning `TooGeneric` or a reported resolution error.
Thin wrapper that packages an already-resolved `Instance` into a `GlobalId` and calls `const_eval_global_id`.

Performs the shared const-value query setup by reveal-all normalizing the parameter environment, combining it with the `GlobalId`, erasing regions for caching, and then calling `eval_to_const_value_raw` directly or via `at(span)` so query errors can be remapped to the provided span.

Evaluates the initializer of a static item after asserting the `DefId` is static. It builds a monomorphic `Instance` with `mono`, wraps it in a `GlobalId`, and then calls `eval_to_allocation` with `ParamEnv::reveal_all()` to obtain the final memory allocation.

Evaluates a `GlobalId` to a concrete memory allocation under a const-enabled parameter environment. Lowers an interpreter operand into a compiler `ConstValue`, preserving zero-sized values, scalar immediates, indirect memory-backed values, and slice-like scalar pairs as appropriate. It explicitly calls `read_immediate` when forcing immediate extraction, falls back to `as_mplace_or_imm`, and for indirect values uses `ptr().into_parts()` to recover the backing allocation; for slice reconstruction it also uses pointer/allocation inspection helpers such as `builtin_deref`, `global_alloc`, and `to_target_usize`.

Reconstructs a `ConstValue` from a previously computed `ConstAlloc` by creating a read-only evaluation context, turning the raw allocation into an interpreter memory place, and then lowering that place back to a `ConstValue`. It explicitly calls `mk_eval_cx_to_read_const_val`, `raw_const_to_mplace`, and `op_to_const`.

Query provider for raw constant values: it evaluates zero-argument intrinsics directly or converts a raw allocation query result into a `ConstValue`. It explicitly calls `eval_nullary_intrinsic` for intrinsic instances, reporting errors via `report`, and otherwise calls `eval_to_allocation_raw` followed by `turn_into_const_value`.

Query provider for raw constant allocations that asserts the request is valid for non-statics/promoteds, checks reveal mode, emits debug tracing, and delegates actual evaluation to the interpreter. It explicitly calls `eval_in_interpreter`.

Returns a fixed diagnostic note explaining that undefined-behavior checks may be overzealous and inviting users to report suspected false positives; it does not meaningfully call other methods in this file.

Builds and returns a compile-time interpreter context for const evaluation by constructing an `InterpCx` with the given type context, span, parameter environment, and static-access policy. Returns whether the const-eval machine stop should be treated as a hard error; it does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
Converts a `ConstEvalErrKind` into `InterpErrorInfo` by wrapping it as a machine-stop interpreter error and then converting it onward; it does not call any other methods from the Methods List.

Formats each `ConstEvalErrKind` variant into a user-facing error message, including specialized text for RFC-gated operations, assertion failures, panics, and aborts; it does not call any other methods from the Methods List.

Constructs a `ConstEvalErr` from interpreter state by printing the backtrace, capturing the generated stacktrace, storing the lowered error kind, and choosing the provided span or the interpreter’s current span; it does not call any other methods from the Methods List.
Builds a hard-error diagnostic wrapper for this const-eval failure and delegates all reporting logic to `impl<'tcx> ConstEvalErr<'tcx>::struct_generic`.
Reports this const-eval failure as an emitted hard error by calling `impl<'tcx> ConstEvalErr<'tcx>::struct_error` with a closure that emits the diagnostic.

Reports this const-eval failure as a lint, optionally replacing the primary span and reattaching previous primary spans as unlabeled secondary labels before emission; it delegates core diagnostic construction to `impl<'tcx> ConstEvalErr<'tcx>::struct_generic`.

Implements the shared diagnostic reporting path for const-eval failures: it adds the main span and multi-frame stacktrace labels, suppresses diagnostics for `TooGeneric`, unknown-layout, and already-reported errors, forces hard errors for layout size overflow, and otherwise emits either a lint or a hard error. Visits an array length, records the span for inferred array lengths, and then continues recursive traversal. It calls `intravisit::walk_array_len`.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Supplies the HIR map used for nested visitor traversal. It calls `self.tcx.hir()`.

Forces collection queries needed by generic parameters, including defaulted type parameters and const parameters/defaults, before recursing into the generics. It calls `self.tcx.hir()`, `self.tcx.ensure().type_of`, `self.tcx.ensure().const_param_default`, and `intravisit::walk_generics`.

Collects interface information for a trait item and then recursively visits its contents. It calls `convert_trait_item` and `intravisit::walk_trait_item`.
Collects interface information for an impl item and then recursively visits its contents. It calls `convert_impl_item` and `intravisit::walk_impl_item`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ba: Creates the base E0121 diagnostic for placeholder `_` appearing in item-signature types, pluralizes the item kind, sorts spans, and labels each offending span. It does not call other methods from the provided list.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Constructs a new `ItemCtxt` from a type context and item `DefId`. It does not call other methods from the list.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ty: Builds the full predicate set for a type parameter by combining inherited bounds from the parent item with bounds written on the current item's generics/where-clause. method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Collects predicates from `where`-clause bound predicates in a `hir::Generics` that apply to a target type or `Self`. Depending on the item, it calls queries like `generics_of`, `type_of`, `predicates_of`, `fn_sig`, `impl_trait_ref`, `trait_def`, `super_predicates_of`, and `explicit_item_bounds`; it also calls `convert_enum_variant_types` for enums, `convert_variant_ctor` for struct/union constructors, and `placeholder_type_error` after visiting items with `HirPlaceholderCollector` when placeholder types in signatures must be rejected.

Forces the interface queries for a trait item and validates illegal placeholder types in trait associated items. Forces the interface queries for an impl item and reports placeholder associated type signatures. Forces collection queries for an enum/struct variant constructor item. It calls `generics_of`, `type_of`, and `predicates_of` on the constructor's local def-id.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ha: Helper for late-bound-region detection on a specific function signature. method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Visits generic parameters to detect whether the target anonymous const appears inside a const parameter's type. For const params, it temporarily marks `in_param_ty` and calls `visit_ty` on the parameter type.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ge: Computes the `ty::Generics` for a local definition by determining its generic parent, handling special cases such as impl/trait items, variant ctors, fields, anonymous consts, opaque types, and closures, and extracting the in-scope parameters. method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::is: Recursively checks whether a HIR type contains `_`-style inference that is suitable for a diagnostic suggestion. It calls itself on nested slice, array, tuple, pointer, reference, and qualified-path components, and calls `are_suggestable_generic_args` to inspect generic argument lists on opaque and path types.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ge: Extracts a function return type only when it is an inferable/suggestable placeholder. It calls `is_suggestable_infer_ty` on `FnRetTy::Return` and returns that type if suggestion logic should handle it.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::fn: Computes the polymorphic function signature for local functions, methods, foreign functions, constructors, variants, and closures. It calls `infer_return_ty_for_fn_sig` for bodies whose return type may be inferred, `AstConv::ty_of_fn` for direct lowering of trait methods or trait impl methods that should not infer returns, `compute_sig_of_foreign_fn_decl` for foreign fns, and for tuple/unit constructors builds a signature from `type_of` on the parent item and fields.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Computes the implemented trait reference for an impl item, if any. It calls `type_of` to obtain the impl self type and `AstConv::instantiate_mono_trait_ref` to lower the HIR trait path into a monomorphic `ty::TraitRef`.

Determines whether an impl is positive, negative, or reservation, and emits errors for invalid uses of `#[rustc_reservation_impl]`. It inspects the impl HIR and attribute state, using `span_err` for disallowed negative or inherent reservation impls.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ea: Iterates the lifetime parameters from a `hir::Generics` that are early-bound rather than late-bound. It filters `generics.params` by calling `is_late_bound` and keeping only lifetime params for which that returns `false`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::pr: Builds the predicates defined directly on `def_id` by starting from `explicit_predicates_of` and, when present, appending `inferred_outlives_of` predicates to the result.
Computes the full predicate set for `def_id` by calling `predicates_defined_on`; if `def_id` is a trait, it also adds the implicit `Self: Trait` predicate.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ga: Collects the explicit predicates written for a local item by inspecting its HIR node, generics, and item kind, setting up trait/default-impl context as needed, and assembling the resulting `GenericPredicates` from the item’s declared bounds and related inherited information.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::co: Traverses a local item to gather `ConstEvaluatable` predicates from anonymous consts. It drives the visitor by calling `visit_trait_ref`, `visit_ty`, `visit_generics`, and `visit_fn_decl` on the relevant HIR pieces, while the visitor’s `visit_anon_const` records each unevaluated anonymous const predicate.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::im: Handles an anonymous const during traversal by converting it to a const value and, if it is unevaluated, inserting a `ConstEvaluatable` predicate for it into the collector.
Intentionally skips visiting const parameter defaults so they do not contribute `ConstEvaluatable` predicates during collection.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::tr: Asserts that the item is a trait and returns its explicit predicates by calling `gather_explicit_predicates_of`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ex: Computes the explicit predicates for `def_id`. For traits, it calls `trait_explicit_predicates_and_bounds` and filters out associated-type bounds that belong in item bounds; otherwise it falls back to `gather_explicit_predicates_of`, with special handling for anon-const/lazy-normalization cases.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::pr: Converts a single HIR generic bound into predicates by calling `add_bounds` on the `AstConv` and then extracting the resulting predicates from the accumulated bounds.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::co: Computes the polymorphic signature of a foreign function declaration by calling `AstConv::ty_of_fn`, choosing intrinsic unsafety when needed via `intrinsic_operation_unsafety`, and then checking the resulting input/output types for gated SIMD FFI usage.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::is: Returns whether a local `def_id` corresponds to a HIR `ForeignItem`, and bugs out if the `DefId` is non-local.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ge: Returns the generator kind for a local closure expression by looking up the closure body and querying its `generator_kind`; returns `None` for non-closure locals and bugs on non-local `DefId`s.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::fr: Parses a `#[target_feature]` attribute, validates each requested feature against the target and enabled feature gates, emits diagnostics for malformed or unsupported entries, and appends accepted features to `target_features`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::li: Maps a textual LLVM linkage name to the corresponding `Linkage` enum value, emitting a fatal error using `def_span` for invalid names.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::co: Collects and validates code generation-related attributes for an item, building a `CodegenFnAttrs` result. It calls `should_inherit_track_caller` to inherit `#[track_caller]`, uses `is_foreign_item` for FFI-only attributes, queries `fn_sig` for ABI-based checks, delegates `#[target_feature]` parsing to `from_target_feature`, resolves linkage strings with `linkage_by_name`, validates ordinals with `check_link_ordinal`, and checks trait-method safety with `check_target_feature_trait_unsafe`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::sh: Determines whether an impl method should inherit `#[track_caller]` from its trait declaration by looking up the associated trait item and calling `codegen_fn_attrs` on that trait item to test for the `TRACK_CALLER` flag.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::ch: Validates and extracts the integer value from a `#[link_ordinal]` attribute, ensuring the attribute shape is correct and that the ordinal fits in `u16`, otherwise emitting diagnostics.
Checks that `#[link_name]` and `#[link_ordinal]` are not both present in the same `CodegenFnAttrs`, emitting an error when both are set.
Rejects `#[target_feature]` on safe trait impl methods by inspecting the enclosing impl item and trait context and emitting an error when the annotated method is not `unsafe`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_typeck/src/collect.rs::st: Returns the mutability of a local `static` or foreign `static` item identified by `def_id`, yielding `Some(mutbl)` for those cases, `None` for other local nodes, and panicking for non-local `DefId`s. It calls `tcx.hir().get_if_local` to look up the local HIR node before matching on `ItemKind::Static` and `ForeignItemKind::Static`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/consts.rs::: Lowers an HIR anonymous const into `ty::Const` by extracting its body and type, trying to eagerly convert literal/parameter forms, and otherwise producing an unevaluated const with identity args. It explicitly calls `hir_node_by_def_id`, `def_span`, `to_def_id`, `hir`, `body`, `type_of`, `no_bound_vars`, `expect`, `Const::try_from_lit_or_param`, `Const::new_unevaluated`, and `identity_for_item`.

Constructs a value constant from raw integer bits by computing the target layout size and wrapping the bits as a scalar `ValTree`. It explicitly calls `layout_of`, `unwrap_or_else`, `Const::new_value`, `from_scalar_int`, `try_from_uint`, and `unwrap`.
Constructs the canonical zero-sized value constant for the given type. It explicitly calls `Const::new_value` and `zst`.
Constructs a boolean constant by forwarding to the raw-bits constructor with the builtin `bool` type. It explicitly calls `Const::from_bits`, `empty`, and `and`.

Evaluates the constant to raw bits by first obtaining a scalar integer and then interpreting it using the constant type's layout size. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar_int` and `self.ty()` from this methods list, while also querying `tcx.layout_of(...)` to determine the bit width.
Evaluates the constant to a boolean by first obtaining a scalar integer and then attempting a boolean conversion. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar_int`.

Evaluates a constant to a `ValTree` when possible: unevaluated consts are prepared and resolved through type-checking const-eval, value consts are returned directly, error consts propagate their error, and param/infer/bound/placeholder/expr consts are rejected as too generic. It explicitly calls `has_escaping_bound_vars`, `Const::kind`, `prepare_for_eval`, `const_eval_resolve_for_typeck`, `dcx`, `span_delayed_bug`, and `into`.
Returns the evaluated raw bits of the constant, panicking with `bug!` if bit evaluation fails. It explicitly calls `try_eval_bits`, and uses `self.ty()` when formatting the failure message.

Retrieves the default value for a local const generic parameter from HIR and wraps it in an `EarlyBinder`. It explicitly calls `Const::from_anon_const` to lower the anonymous constant after locating the default const definition.

Builds a `Const` from an anonymous const argument definition by fetching the HIR anon-const body, computing its type, and first calling `try_eval_lit_or_param` to eagerly turn literal or const-parameter expressions into a concrete const. If that returns `None`, it falls back to interning an `Unevaluated` const with `mk_const`.

Attempts to convert an expression into a constant immediately. It unwraps trivial blocks, recognizes literal and negated-literal expressions and lowers them through `lit_to_const`, and recognizes resolved const-parameter paths to construct a `Param` const via `mk_const`. Returns `Some(Const)` for those supported cases and `None` otherwise.

Builds a `Const` for an inline anonymous const by retrieving its HIR body and inferred type, then calling `try_eval_lit_or_param` to eagerly materialize literals or const parameters. If that fails, it creates an `Unevaluated` inline-const with the appropriate substituted parent context using `mk_const`, and finally asserts the result has no free regions.
Constructs and interns a constant from an already computed `ConstValue` and type by calling `mk_const` with `ConstKind::Value`.
Constructs a scalar constant by wrapping the `Scalar` as `ConstValue::Scalar` and calling `from_value`.
Constructs a target-`usize` constant from a `u64` by calling `from_bits` with the `usize` type under an empty `ParamEnv`.
Attempts to evaluate this constant to a machine `usize` by calling `self.val.eval` and then `try_to_machine_usize` on the evaluated value.
Evaluates this constant to a `u64` usize value by calling `try_eval_usize` and unwrapping the result, panicking with `bug!` if evaluation does not yield a usize.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/build/mod.r: Main MIR-construction dispatcher for a body owner. It queries HIR/typeck state, forces prerequisite unsafety and abstract-const analyses, identifies the body/return-type span from HIR, then builds an inference context and dispatches to either `construct_fn`, `construct_const`, or `construct_error` depending on the item kind and whether THIR/typeck construction failed.

Computes the closure environment type with late-bound regions liberated for MIR building. It reads the closure type from `tcx.typeck_body(body_id).node_type`, derives the environment type with `tcx.closure_env_ty`, and erases the late-bound region binder with `tcx.erase_late_bound_regions`.
Returns whether this block frame represents a tail-expression context by pattern-matching on `BlockFrame::TailExpr`.
Returns whether this block frame represents a statement context by pattern-matching on `BlockFrame::Statement`.
Checks whether a local variable id is currently tracked in any active match-guard frame by scanning `guard_context` with nested iterator `any` tests.
Maps a THIR local-variable id to the MIR local to use in the current guard mode. It calls `LocalsForNode::local_id` on the entry stored in `self.var_indices`.
Creates an empty `BlockContext` with no active block frames.
Pushes a `BlockFrame` onto the block-context stack.
Pops and returns the most recent `BlockFrame` from the block-context stack.
Finds the nearest enclosing tail-expression frame that is not masked by a statement frame by iterating the block-context stack in reverse, and returns its tail-result metadata if present.
Reports whether the current block context should ignore a tail expression's result, based on the last active frame in the stack.
Constructs a `GuardFrameLocal` that records only the bound local variable id for guard tracking.

Selects the MIR local to use for a binding, choosing between the ordinary local and the guard-specific reference local depending on `ForGuard`, and bugs if a single-local binding is incorrectly requested from within a guard.
Trait method that combines a basic block with an arbitrary value into a `BlockAnd<T>` pair.
Trait method that converts a basic block into a `BlockAnd<()>` pair carrying unit.
Wraps this `BasicBlock` and a supplied value into `BlockAnd<T>`.
Wraps this `BasicBlock` into `BlockAnd<()>` with a unit payload.

Builds MIR for a function or closure body. It collects arguments, creates a `Builder` with `Builder::new`, enters call-site and argument scopes via `builder.in_scope`, enters the return breakable scope with `builder.in_breakable_scope`, lowers parameters and the body by calling `builder.args_and_body`, emits the final return terminator with `builder.cfg.terminate`, finalizes drops with `builder.build_drop_trees`, uses `return_block.unit()` to package the scope result, and completes the MIR with `builder.finish`.

Builds MIR for a constant or static initializer. It creates a `Builder` with `Builder::new`, lowers the THIR expression into the return place by calling `builder.expr_into_dest`, emits a `Return` terminator with `builder.cfg.terminate`, runs `builder.build_drop_trees`, and returns the finished body from `builder.finish`.

Constructs fallback error MIR for items whose earlier compilation stages failed. It computes parameter count from HIR, creates minimal CFG/source-scope/local-decl state, adds parameter locals, terminates the start block as `Unreachable` with `cfg.terminate`, builds the body with `Body::new`, and records a generator yield type when applicable.

Initializes the MIR `Builder` state for a body, computing overflow-check behavior, parameter/typeck/region context, CFG and local tables, and other bookkeeping. It also initializes the CFG start block with `builder.cfg.start_new_block` and creates the outermost source scope by calling `builder.new_source_scope`.
Finalizes MIR construction. It validates that every basic block has a terminator by iterating the CFG, then creates the finished MIR body with `Body::new`.

Allocates MIR locals for function arguments, records argument debug info, prepares closure/generator capture metadata and upvar debug info when needed, schedules capture drops, and lowers argument patterns and the function body into MIR. During argument lowering it calls `self.set_correct_source_scope_for_arg` to adjust lint/source scopes for each argument pattern.

Adjusts the current source scope when an argument pattern belongs to a different lint-level root than its parent scope. If the roots differ, it creates a replacement scope by calling `self.new_source_scope`.
Returns a cached temporary place for unit values, creating it on first use by calling `self.temp` with `tcx.mk_unit()` and then storing the result in `self.unit_temp`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_build/src/thir/cx/blo: Lowers a block’s HIR statements into THIR statement IDs by iterating in order, skipping item statements, translating expression/semi statements into `StmtKind::Expr`, and translating `let` statements into THIR let-statements with destruction/remainder scope information, lowered patterns, optional user type ascription, initializer handling, and optional `else` block lowering. It explicitly calls `mirror_expr` for statement initializers/expressions, `pattern_from_hir` for `let` patterns, and recursively calls `mirror_stmts` when lowering nested statement structure.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_passes/src/liveness.rs::l: Formats a `LiveNodeKind` into a human-readable diagnostic string using the source map for span-based variants, and returns fixed owned strings for `ClosureNode` and `ExitNode`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_passes/src/liveness.rs::c: Runs the liveness pass over all item-like nodes in a module by creating `IrMaps` with `IrMaps::new` and visiting the module through `as_deep_visitor`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_passes/src/liveness.rs::p: Registers this file’s query provider by installing `check_mod_liveness` into `Providers`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_passes/src/liveness.rs::i: Constructs a fresh `IrMaps` with the given type context and empty maps/vectors for live nodes, variables, captures, and variable metadata.
Appends a new `LiveNodeKind` to the live-node table, returning its compact `LiveNode` index. It calls `live_node_kind_to_string` for debug logging.
Creates and records a live node for a specific `HirId` by calling `add_live_node`, then storing the resulting index in `live_node_map`.
Appends a new variable description to `var_kinds`, returning its `Variable` index, and for locals, parameters, and upvars also records the `HirId` to variable mapping in `variable_map`.
Looks up the `Variable` index associated with a `HirId` in `variable_map`, and reports a span bug if no variable was registered.
Returns the symbol name stored for the given variable, regardless of whether it is a local, parameter, or upvar.
Reports whether a variable came from shorthand struct-pattern syntax; this is tracked only for locals, while parameters and upvars always return false.
Associates a closure expression `HirId` with its capture information by storing the capture list in `capture_info_map`.

Traverses a pattern iteratively and collects the `HirId`s of bindings introduced through shorthand struct fields, descending through nested binding, struct, ref/box, tuple, or-pattern, and slice patterns.

Registers all bindings in a pattern as tracked locals. It calls `collect_shorthand_field_ids` to detect shorthand bindings, then for each binding calls `add_live_node_for_node` to create a `VarDefNode` and `add_variable` to record the corresponding `Local`.
Provides the HIR map used for nested visitor traversal by returning `self.tcx.hir()`.

Main per-body entry for AST liveness setup: it creates fresh maps with `IrMaps::new`, skips derived impls and `#[naked]` bodies, registers mentioned upvars with `add_variable`, walks the body to collect nodes, then builds `Liveness` with `Liveness::new` and runs analysis via `compute`, `log_liveness`, `visit_body`, `warn_about_unused_upvars`, and `warn_about_unused_args`.
Processes a local declaration by first registering bindings from its pattern with `add_from_pat`, then continuing recursive traversal with `walk_local`.
Processes a match arm by registering bindings from the arm pattern with `add_from_pat`, also registering `if let` guard bindings with `add_from_pat` when present, and then recursing with `walk_arm`.

Registers each parameter binding as a tracked variable, using `collect_shorthand_field_ids` to preserve shorthand-struct information and `add_variable` to store either a `Local` for struct-pattern parameters or a `Param` otherwise, then recurses with `walk_param`.

Creates liveness IR for expressions that matter to dataflow and control flow. It calls `add_live_node_for_node` for local-path uses, closures, `let` expressions, and control-flow/significant expressions; for closures it also calls `add_live_node` to create per-upvar `UpvarNode`s and `set_captures` to record capture metadata; for `let` expressions it calls `add_from_pat`; and in all handled cases it continues traversal with `walk_expr`.

Constructs the liveness analysis state for one body: fetches type checking results and parameter environment, looks up closure capture info, creates distinguished closure and exit nodes by calling `IrMaps::add_live_node`, and allocates successor and read/write/use tables sized from the collected IR.
Looks up the `LiveNode` assigned to a `HirId` in the IR maps, and reports a span bug if the node was not registered during IR construction.
Delegates variable lookup to `IrMaps::variable` for the given `HirId` and span.

Propagates liveness backward through pattern bindings, considering only the first branch of an or-pattern. For each binding it calls `live_node` to find the binding node, `variable` to find the tracked variable, `init_from_succ` to copy successor state, and `define` to mark the binding as defined, returning the updated predecessor node.
Returns whether a variable is live on entry to a node by querying the RWU table’s reader bit.
Returns whether a variable is live on exit from a node by following the stored successor and calling `live_on_entry` on that successor.
Returns whether a variable is marked as used on entry to a node by querying the RWU table’s use bit.
Returns whether a variable is assigned on entry to a node by querying the RWU table’s writer bit.
Returns whether a variable is assigned on exit from a node by following the stored successor and calling `assigned_on_entry` on that successor.
Writes all variable indices satisfying a supplied predicate to an output stream by iterating over the tracked variable range and testing each `Variable`.
Builds a debug string describing one live node, including its kind, read/write/use sets, and successor. It calls `write_vars` three times to print the reader, writer, and used variable subsets.
Logs the computed liveness state for a body by iterating over all live-node entries in `self.ir.lnks` and formatting each with `ln_str` after converting indices with `LiveNode::from`.
Initializes a live node’s successor edge to `succ_ln` without changing RWU state, relying on the table’s initially empty entries.
Initializes a live node from an existing successor by setting the successor edge and copying RWU state from `succ_ln`; calls `self.rwu_table.copy` and uses `ln_str` for debug output.
Merges RWU information from `succ_ln` into `ln`, returning whether anything changed; calls `self.rwu_table.union` and uses `ln_str` for debug output.
Marks a variable as defined at `writer` by clearing read/write bits while preserving prior use information; calls `self.rwu_table.get_used` and `self.rwu_table.set`, and logs with `ln_str`.
Applies read/write/use access flags for a variable at a live node, updating the RWU entry in place; calls `self.rwu_table.get` and `self.rwu_table.set`, and uses `ln_str` for debug output.

Computes body liveness starting from the body expression, first marking captured-by-reference upvars as read/used on closure exit, then propagating through the body, and for `Fn`/`FnMut` closures extending liveness of captured bindings back to entry. It calls `variable`, `acc`, `propagate_through_expr`, `init_from_succ`, `define`, and `merge_from_succ`.

Propagates liveness backward through a block by recording `break` targets, then processing the tail expression and statements in reverse order. It calls `propagate_through_opt_expr` and `propagate_through_stmt`.

Propagates liveness through a statement, handling locals by first propagating through the initializer and then defining pattern bindings, leaving items unchanged, and propagating through expression/semi statements. It calls `propagate_through_opt_expr`, `define_bindings_in_pat`, and `propagate_through_expr`.
Propagates liveness backward through a slice of expressions in reverse evaluation order; calls `propagate_through_expr` for each expression.
Propagates liveness through an optional expression when present; calls `propagate_through_expr` for `Some(expr)` and otherwise returns `succ` unchanged.

Core backward transfer function for expressions: dispatches on expression kind to model reads, writes, control-flow joins, closures, loops, yields, assignments, and composite expressions. Depending on the case it calls `access_path`, `init_from_succ`, `variable`, `acc`, `define_bindings_in_pat`, `propagate_through_loop`, `live_node`, `merge_from_succ`, `propagate_through_opt_expr`, `init_empty`, `write_place`, `propagate_through_place_components`, and `propagate_through_exprs`.

Propagates through the subcomponents of a non-tracked place, ignoring direct writes to complex places and instead reading the relevant base expressions. It calls `propagate_through_expr` for field bases and for general fallback cases.
Handles writes to tracked places by recognizing local-variable paths and forwarding them as accesses; calls `access_path` for resolved path places and otherwise leaves `succ` unchanged.
Creates or finds the live node for a variable access, links it to the successor, and records the requested access bits. It calls `live_node`, `init_from_succ`, `variable`, and `acc`.
Converts a resolved local path into a variable access and otherwise ignores non-local paths; calls `access_var` for `Res::Local`.

Builds the backward-flow model for a loop, installs break/continue targets, propagates through the body, and iterates to a fixed point by merging the body back into the loop header. It calls `live_node`, `init_empty`, `propagate_through_block`, and `merge_from_succ`.

Checks whether an expression’s type is uninhabited in the current module and, if so, warns about the successor node being unreachable and redirects control to `exit_ln`. It calls `warn_about_unreachable` when the successor is an expression or variable-definition node.
Emits an `UNREACHABLE_CODE` lint for code made unreachable by an expression of uninhabited type, skipping the special case of `!` to avoid duplicate diagnostics.

Checks local-pattern bindings for unused variables and dead initial assignments, then continues normal HIR traversal. It calls `check_unused_vars_in_pat`, may call `warn_about_dead_assign` via the callback, and then calls `intravisit::walk_local`.
Runs liveness-specific expression checks and then recursively visits subexpressions. It calls `check_expr` and `intravisit::walk_expr`.
Checks arm-pattern bindings for unused variables before continuing traversal. It calls `check_unused_vars_in_pat` and `intravisit::walk_arm`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_passes/src/liveness.rs::c: Per-expression diagnostic checker that validates assignment targets, inline-asm output places, and `let`-pattern unused bindings, while ignoring expression kinds with no extra liveness-specific checks. It calls `check_place` and `check_unused_vars_in_pat`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_passes/src/liveness.rs::i: Checks whether assigning to a place corresponds to a local variable assignment that should be diagnosed as dead, otherwise recursively walks embedded rvalue subexpressions. It calls `live_node`, `variable`, `warn_about_dead_assign`, and `intravisit::walk_expr`.
Returns the variable name to use in warnings unless the binding is anonymous or underscore-prefixed, in which case it suppresses the warning.

Emits unused-variable or unused-assignment lints for captured-by-value upvars based on whether they are used or live on closure entry. It calls `variable`, `used_on_entry`, `live_on_entry`, and `should_warn`.

Checks each function parameter pattern for arguments whose passed-in value is never read. It calls `check_unused_vars_in_pat`, queries `live_on_entry` in the callback, and calls `report_unused_assign` for unused incoming values.

Collects bindings in a pattern, coalescing same-named bindings across or-pattern alternatives, then either invokes the provided callback for bindings used on entry or reports them as unused. It calls `live_node`, `variable`, `used_on_entry`, `report_unused`, and the supplied `on_used_on_entry` callback.

Emits the appropriate unused-variable diagnostic and suggestions for a binding, distinguishing between never-used bindings and bindings only written, and tailoring suggestions for shorthand patterns. It calls `should_warn`, `assigned_on_exit`, and `variable`.
Reports an assignment whose written value is never subsequently live. It calls `live_on_exit` and `report_unused_assign`.

Emits an `UNUSED_ASSIGNMENTS` lint for an assignment whose value is never read, but only when `should_warn` returns a visible variable name for the given `Variable`. It explicitly calls `should_warn`, and on success uses `struct_span_lint_hir` to build the diagnostic, invokes the supplied `message` closure to format the main message, then finalizes the lint with `help` and `emit`.

related_methods.reason: This is the main entry point on the crashing path: the stack trace explicitly includes `rustc_trait_selection::traits::const_evaluatable::is_const_evaluatable` during well-formedness checking of the const generic default. Its documented behavior includes falling back to `const_eval_resolve` for unevaluated consts, which matches the query stack (`eval_to_const_value_raw` / `eval_to_allocation_raw`). A bug here could incorrectly force evaluation of an erroneous anon const containing an uninitialized local instead of short-circuiting with a normal diagnostic.

The reproducer uses an anonymous const as a default const generic expression on a type definition. This function specifically computes THIR-based abstract consts for eligible anonymous consts and inline consts, so it is directly involved in deciding whether the const is represented abstractly or sent down another path. If it fails to reject or properly classify this block expression, `is_const_evaluatable` may incorrectly fall through to eager const evaluation and ICE.

This builder initializer decides whether a THIR body is polymorphic and thus whether an abstract const should be built at all. Since the failing const generic default is an anon const in item syntax, a misclassification here could cause the compiler to skip abstract-const handling and instead eagerly evaluate invalid MIR. That makes it a plausible root cause in the handoff between generic-const analysis and const-eval.

The reproducer’s default is a block expression with local statements and a method call, exactly the kind of nontrivial THIR shape this recursive lowering must either support or reject. If it mishandles blocks, locals, or method-call lowering inside anon consts, it could fail to produce a safe abstract representation and allow later const-eval on an invalid body, leading to the observed ICE.

This is the final step that constructs and validates the abstract-const node slice after recursive lowering. If the bug is due to missing validation of unsupported forms in the const generic default, this method is a likely place where the compiler should have rejected the expression before `is_const_evaluatable` reached `const_eval_resolve`.

Most suspicious because it explicitly validates generic defaults, including const parameter defaults (`const_param_default` appears in its calls), and the ICE occurs while checking well-formedness of a struct with a default const generic.
